terms.comment: Literally “don’t copy out from the one next to you”. Exscrībō is the classical word for copying out a text (Cic. Verr. 2.2.189, Lewis & Short), but we have found no classical instance of it for copying in a test; the phrase is Traupman’s.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
